text: A deposit into a new account credits it and records a deposit entry. Given a new Ledger with no accounts; when deposit('A', 100, 't1') is called; then the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') is 100 and entries('A') is one entry { txnId: 't1', kind: 'deposit', amount: 100 }.

An unknown account reads as balance 0 with no entries. Given a new Ledger where account 'X' has never been used; when balance('X') and entries('X') are read; then balance('X') is 0 and entries('X') is an empty list.

Opening an account that already exists does not reset it. Given account 'A' holds 100 after deposit('A', 100, 't1'); when open('A') is called again; then balance('A') stays 100 and its single deposit entry is kept.

Deposit amounts are rounded to the nearest cent, with half a cent rounding up. Given a new Ledger; when deposit('A', 0.125, 't1') is called; then the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') is 0.13 and the entry amount is 0.13.
Deposit amounts with a third decimal below 5 round down to the cent. Given a new Ledger; when deposit('A', 1.234, 't1') is called; then balance('A') is 1.23.

A deposit smaller than half a cent is accepted but records an amount of 0. Given a new Ledger; when deposit('A', 0.004, 't1') is called; then the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') is 0 and one deposit entry with amount 0 is recorded.

Withdrawing one cent more than the balance is rejected. Given account 'A' holds 100; when withdraw('A', 100.01, 'w1') is called; then the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' } and balance('A') stays 100.

Withdrawing more than the balance is rejected and the balance is unchanged. Given account 'A' holds 100; when withdraw('A', 150, 'w1') is called; then the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' } and balance('A') stays 100.

Withdrawing from an account that was never funded is rejected as insufficient-funds. Given a new Ledger; when withdraw('Z', 10, 'w1') is called; then the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' } and balance('Z') is 0.

A txnId already used by a deposit makes a withdrawal with that txnId a silent no-op. Given deposit('A', 100, 't1') has succeeded; when withdraw('A', 40, 't1') is called with the same txnId; then the result is { ok: true } but balance('A') stays 100 and no withdrawal entry is recorded.

A rejected withdrawal does not use up its txnId, so it can be retried later. Given account 'A' holds 50 and withdraw('A', 100, 'w1') was rejected for insufficient-funds, then deposit('A', 50, 'd2') brought the balance to 100; when withdraw('A', 100, 'w1') is retried; then the result is { ok: true } and balance('A') becomes 0.

Withdrawing exactly the daily limit of 5000 in one go is allowed. Given account 'A' holds 10000 and has not withdrawn anything; when withdraw('A', 5000, 'w1') is called; then the result is { ok: true } and balance('A') becomes 5000.

Withdrawing one cent over the daily limit of 5000 is rejected. Given account 'A' holds 10000 and has not withdrawn anything; when withdraw('A', 5000.01, 'w1') is called; then the result is { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' } and balance('A') stays 10000.

The daily limit is cumulative across withdrawals on the same account. Given account 'A' holds 10000 and has already withdrawn 3000 and then 2000 (5000 in total); when withdraw('A', 0.01, 'w3') is called; then the result is { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' } and balance('A') stays 5000.

A withdrawal rejected by the daily limit does not count toward the limit. Given account 'A' holds 10000, withdrew 4000, then had withdraw 2000 rejected for daily-limit; when withdraw('A', 1000, 'w3') is called; then the result is { ok: true } and balance('A') becomes 5000.

The daily limit is tracked separately per account. Given accounts 'A' and 'B' each hold 10000 and 'A' has withdrawn 5000; when withdraw('B', 5000, 'wb') is called; then the result is { ok: true } and balance('B') becomes 5000.

Insufficient funds is reported before the daily limit when both apply. Given account 'A' holds 100; when withdraw('A', 6000, 'w1') is called; then the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }.

Transfers are not subject to or counted toward the daily withdrawal limit. Given account 'A' holds 20000; when transfer('A', 'B', 8000, 't1') is called, then withdraw('A', 5000, 'w1'); then both succeed: balance('A') becomes 7000 and balance('B') becomes 8000.

A withdrawal amount is rounded to cents before the balance check. Given account 'A' holds 1; when withdraw('A', 0.999, 'w1') is called; then the amount rounds to 1, the result is { ok: true } and balance('A') becomes 0.

A transfer moves money between accounts and records an entry on each side. Given account 'A' holds 100 and 'B' has never been used; when transfer('A', 'B', 40, 't1') is called; then the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') is 60, balance('B') is 40, 'A' gets a transfer-out entry of 40 and 'B' gets a transfer-in entry of 40.

Transferring exactly the whole balance is allowed. Given account 'A' holds 100; when transfer('A', 'B', 100, 't1') is called; then the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') is 0 and balance('B') is 100.

Transferring one cent more than the balance is rejected and nothing moves. Given account 'A' holds 100; when transfer('A', 'B', 100.01, 't1') is called; then the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }, balance('A') stays 100, balance('B') stays 0 and no transfer entries are recorded.

A transfer from an account to itself is accepted, leaves the balance unchanged and records two entries. Given account 'A' holds 100; when transfer('A', 'A', 30, 't1') is called; then the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') stays 100, and entries('A') gains a transfer-out of 30 then a transfer-in of 30.

Transfer amounts are rounded to the nearest cent, with half a cent rounding up. Given account 'A' holds 1; when transfer('A', 'B', 0.125, 't1') is called; then balance('B') is 0.13 and the transfer-in entry amount is 0.13.

The list returned by entries is a copy; changing it does not change the ledger's history. Given account 'A' has one deposit entry; when the caller empties the array returned by entries('A') and reads entries('A') again; then entries('A') still has 1 entry.
